ev.q: Influenza vaccination coverage was 79.9% during the 2021–22 season, and 87.3% of HCP reported having completed the primary COVID-19 vaccination series
Percentage point change in weighted % vaccinated, 2020–21 to 2021–22 (95% CI)
Receipt of ≥1 COVID-19 vaccine dose, completion of primary series, and receipt of 1 COVID-19 booster dose among health care personnel
Overall, 89.9% of HCP reported having received ≥1 dose of a COVID-19 vaccine, and 87.3% reported having completed the primary COVID-19 vaccination series
Among HCP who reported employer vaccination requirements, influenza vaccination coverage ranged from 95.8% to 97.3%
Among HCP who reported that their employer neither recommended nor required vaccinations, influenza vaccination coverage ranged from 40.1% to 64.2%
Overall, 79.9% of HCP reported having received an influenza vaccination during the 2021–22 season, not significantly different from the 75.9% reported during the 2020–21 season
During March 29–April 19, 2022, CDC conducted an opt-in Internet panel survey of 3,618 U.S. HCP
Overall, 79.9% of HCP reported having received an influenza vaccination during the 2021–22 season, not significantly different from the 75.9% reported during the 2020–21 season

methods_quotes.q: The Korn-Graubard method was used to calculate CIs for proportions, assuming that the weighted estimates were approximately unbiased.
A poststratification weight for each survey respondent was calculated by fitting a generalized exponential model and estimating the model parameters using calibration equations
T-tests were used to assess differences among subgroups; p<0.05 was considered statistically significant.
CDC’s National Center for Health Statistics reliability criteria for proportions were applied to the estimates in the descriptive analyses of HCP characteristics
The difference between percentages is based on unrounded percentages in each season.
